sources.title: Library of Congress, Country Profile: South Korea (May 2005)
sources.note: Direct PDF, historical background pp. 1 and 4 to 5 and government section. Used for historical chronology only; officeholders and statistics in this 2005 profile are not treated as current.

sources.title: U.S. National Archives, Korean War Armistice Agreement, 1953
sources.note: Direct original article, paragraphs on 25 June 1950, 27 July 1953 and the four-kilometer demilitarized zone. The image caption says July 23, but the agreement and article text establish July 27; this card follows the latter.

sources.title: Korea Legislation Research Institute, Constitution of the Republic of Korea, amended 29 October 1987
sources.note: Direct English translation. Articles 1, 3, 4, 31, 36, 67 and 70. Normative legal provisions are distinguished from measured social outcomes.

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World, Archives of the May 18th Democratic Uprising
sources.note: Original indexed institutional description: uprising 18 to 27 May 1980, documents, photographs and images concerning the uprising, punishment and compensation; registered 2011.

sources.title: Constitutional Court of Korea, Case 2024Hun-Na8: President Yoon impeachment, 4 April 2025
sources.note: Original indexed decision announcement, also confirmed in direct official Case Search results. Finding is removal from office; not a criminal sentence. English summaries are informational; Korean decision is authoritative.

sources.title: Constitutional Court of Korea, Newsletter: Second Half of 2024
sources.note: Original indexed court newsletter records 3 December 2024 martial-law declaration and impeachment case filed 14 December. Combined conservatively with the subsequent case announcement as one underlying work for budgeting.

sources.title: Haggard, Kim and Moon, The transition to export-led growth in South Korea: 1954 to 1966, World Bank WPS 546
sources.note: Original indexed abstract and publication metadata, 30 November 1990; direct page returns Loading. Restricted to the abstract-supported early-1960s shift from import substitution to export-oriented industry and institutional/political analysis.

sources.title: IMF, Stand-by Credit for Korea, Press Release 97/55, 4 December 1997
sources.note: Original release: SDR 15.5 billion, approximately US$21 billion, three-year arrangement; SDR 4.1 billion immediately available. The IMF commitment is not confused with the wider rescue package.

sources.title: Seoul Museum of History, Exhibit 431: Seocho Samho Apartment
sources.note: Original indexed bilingual curatorial text: apartment complex 1978, family of four from 1981 for thirty years, collected before 2014 demolition, furniture donated, additions and altered display floor plan explicitly acknowledged.

sources.title: Seoul Museum of History, Exhibit 430: Living in an Apartment
sources.note: Original indexed bilingual curatorial text: Mapo complex 1962, apartment districts 1976, Gangnam development. These are Seoul examples, not a claim that every household lived in an apartment.

sources.title: UNESCO, Kimjang: making and sharing kimchi in the Republic of Korea, file 00881
sources.note: Original indexed nomination summary, inscription 2013. Annual preparation calendar, autumn cooperation and sharing, family transmission. Registration date does not date the origin of the practice.

sources.title: UNESCO, Culture of Jeju haenyeo women divers, file 01068
sources.note: Original indexed description, inscription 2016. Breath-hold diving to ten meters, sea harvest, senior experience groups and intergenerational transmission. No claim that children should imitate diving.

sources.title: UNESCO, Haenyeo schools: safeguarding knowledge and skills, Article 18 case study 18
sources.note: Original indexed community-consented safeguarding account, including one-to-one mentoring, ecology/safety lessons and museum miniature tools. Contemporary teaching, not evidence that such schools existed throughout the twentieth century. Grouped with file 01068 conservatively.

sources.title: OECD, PISA 2022 Results: Korea country note
sources.note: Original country note, 5 December 2023. Sample 6,454 fifteen-year-olds in 186 schools; performance, belonging and life satisfaction sections. Survey estimates, not universal claims about Korean children.

sources.title: WHO Asia Pacific Observatory, Republic of Korea health system review, ISBN 9789290617105
sources.note: Original indexed review overview, posted 28 May 2017, underlying 2015 review. Universal coverage 1989; early-2000s insurer merger and prescribing/dispensing separation; private delivery and household cost limitations. Historical findings are dated.

sources.title: Seoul Sewerage Science Museum, History of Korean sewerage
sources.note: Original indexed Korean museum essay: urban river pollution and first urban sewage treatment plant, Cheonggyecheon, 1976. Direct extraction omits parts available in the original indexed text; exact query site:sssmuseum.seoul.kr "1976" "청계천" verified.

sources.title: Korea Tourism Organization, Haewoojae collection entry
sources.note: Original Korean institutional description: Sim Jae-duck, toilet-shaped house designed by Ko Gi-woong, completed 2007, later donated to Suwon and made an exhibition space with children’s activities. No international Guinness claim reproduced.

sources.title: Korea Aerospace Research Institute, Second Nuri launch succeeds, 21 June 2022
sources.note: Direct original launch report: performance-verification satellite reached target orbit and communicated with ground station.

sources.title: Korea Aerospace Research Institute, Korean Launch Vehicle NURI
sources.note: Original indexed institutional engineering description: first launch failed to achieve orbital speed, second succeeded, 3.5-meter propellant tank with wall thickness two to three millimeters; exact query site:kari.re.kr "propellant tank" "2~3". Grouped with launch release conservatively.

sources.title: Nobel Prize, Han Kang: 2024 biobibliography
sources.note: Original indexed Nobel text verified under this URL with sfnsn=mo query mirror; direct fetch intermittently fails. Lists 채식주의자 (2007; The Vegetarian, 2015), Korean bibliography and translators. Swedish PDF of the same bibliography independently confirms original script and 2007 date; counted as the same work.

sources.title: Swedish Academy, Nobel Prize in Literature 2024 announcement
sources.note: Official original indexed press release awards Han Kang the prize for poetic prose engaging historical trauma and human fragility. Conservatively grouped with biobibliography as one Nobel packet.

proposedOverrides.name: South Korea
proposedOverrides.summary: The modern southern republic, founded in 1948, with a map record beginning in 1960.

batchIdentityNotes.text: Indexed from 1960 with no end. Historical Republic of Korea established 15 August 1948. Decoded world-1960, world-1994, world-2000 and world-2010 features all bbox [124.610,33.194,130.921,38.625]. Separate from korea-usa and northern Korean states; no aliases added. Outline is neither all Korean cultural space nor adjudication of territorial claims. Last detailed political event is 4 April 2025; no current officeholder assertion. Period end 2026 is exclusive display chronology, not a predicted end of state.
